answers.rationale: I'm genuinely interested in using AI for code edits, but only with full visibility. Inline diffs are exactly what I need to trust the tool. Without that review step, I'd be nervous, but with it, I'm quite willing to adopt this.

Checkpoint rollback is a game-changer for me. Knowing I can undo autonomous changes instantly removes my biggest friction point. That safety net makes me comfortable delegating complex tasks I'd otherwise hesitate on.

My top worry is that the agent introduces subtle bugs or logic errors that pass initial review but break production. Diffs help, but AI can still make plausible-looking mistakes that are hard to catch without running tests.

answers.value: Refactoring variable names and extracting utility functions in a well-tested module with good test coverage
answers.rationale: I'd start with low-risk refactoring tasks where changes are mechanical and easy to verify. Tests will catch any breakage, and the scope is contained. Once I build confidence, I'd move to more complex autonomous edits.
